title: Recent Decision Not to Recommend Those Aged 60 to 75 to Take Second COVID-19 Booster Shot
what_it_is: Recent Decision Not to Recommend Those Aged 60 to 75 to Take Second COVID-19 Booster Shot

sections.label: COVID-19 vaccination recommendations and safety
sections.summary: Seniors 60 and above and medically vulnerable persons should get the updated bivalent booster about one year after their last dose, with serious adverse event rates lower for second boosters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The current recommendation for COVID-19 vaccination is for seniors aged 60 years and above, and medically vulnerable persons, to achieve minimum protection and receive the updated bivalent booster around one year after their last booster dose.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Instead of counting doses, the current phrasing better communicates the recommendation for the longer term: to have regular doses and maintain immunity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: COVID-19 vaccines offered under the National Vaccination Programme have been assessed to be safe for use and the benefits of such vaccines continue to outweigh the associated risks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: As of 31 May 2023, based on the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) surveillance, the serious adverse event rate of the mRNA COVID-19 vaccines in Singapore was two in 100,000 doses for the second booster dose, lower than nine in 100,000 and four in 100,000 for the primary and first booster doses respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The bivalent mRNA vaccines against the Omicron strain currently offered under the National Vaccination Programme are the most updated formulations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The same Committee also recommended manufacturers to produce updated vaccines targeting the XBB sublineage of the Omicron variant ahead of the Northern Hemisphere fall season.

sections.label: Contracts for latest vaccines
sections.summary: Contracts enable procurement of the latest vaccines if assessed appropriate for the local situation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Our contracts enable us to procure the latest vaccines, should they be assessed to be appropriate for our local situation.

sections.label: Continued elderly booster recommendation
sections.summary: The elderly are still recommended to receive COVID-19 vaccine doses one year after their last booster, starting from five months after, and to receive the bivalent vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And I hope he will also help to dispel the misconception that we no longer recommend that second booster dose for the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We continue to recommend that the elderly continue to receive doses of COVID-19 vaccines and that they receive it one year after their last booster dose, and they can start to receive it from five months after their last booster dose, and persons are recommended to receive the bivalent vaccine.
